page: OVHcloud a10-45 is a GPU-accelerated server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 30 dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9554 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 3.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 42.0 GB of system memory, which equates to a relatively low ratio of 1.4 GB per core. For acceleration, the server is equipped with a single NVIDIA A10 GPU based on the Ampere architecture, providing 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage consists of a 400 GB SSD, and the network interface delivers an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance characteristics across multiple domains. The AMD EPYC processor achieves top 25% results in both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, as well as Passmark CPU and database operations. Memory performance is mixed, showing top 25% throughput for small cached blocks but falling into the middle 50% for larger uncached read and write operations. The integrated NVIDIA A10 GPU delivers top 10% performance for LLM inference tasks using small (135M) and medium (7B) models. However, for larger 70B models, while prompt processing remains strong, text generation speed drops to the bottom 10%, highlighting a hardware limitation when handling massive model parameters.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the a10-45 offers a dense compute and graphics profile, making it a viable option for specialized workloads without the overhead of larger multi-GPU systems. The primary tradeoff is the low memory-to-vCPU ratio, which may limit memory-intensive applications. This server is highly suited for mid-sized LLM inference, machine learning model training, 3D rendering, software compilation, and database operations that benefit from dedicated CPU cores and GPU acceleration.
